# Gijjhajātaka (Ja 427)

**ID:** Ja 427
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Gijjhajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul8.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In the text and commentary edited by V. Fausböll, it forms the first story of the *Navakanipāta*, immediately following the close of the *Aṭṭhanipāta* [Fausböll 1883]. The framing narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*) is set at Jetavana near Sāvatthī and was spoken by the Buddha concerning an unruly or disobedient monk (*dubbaca bhikkhu*) who failed to heed the admonitions and instructions of his teachers, preceptors, and companions in the holy life regarding monastic deportment [Fausböll 1883]. The opening verse incipit is recorded as *Parisamkupatho nāmā 'ti* (“Formed of rough logs...”) [Fausböll 1883].

**Sources**

- [Fausböll 1883] V. Fausböll, Jataka Together with Its Commentary, Vol. 3 (1883) — Pali opening incipit, nidāna context of the dubbaca monk, and nipāta placement.
